title.zh: 卷十二 志第四 天文上
title.raw: 卷十二 志第四 天文上 Volume 12 Treatises 4: Astronomy 1

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷十二‧志第四

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, volume twelve, treatise four
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, volume 12, treatise 4

sentences.zh: 天文上

translations.literal: Astronomy, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy 1

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「聖人仰觀象於天，俯觀法於地。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 「The sage looked up to observe patterns in Heaven and looked down to observe models on Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 「The sage looked up to read Heaven's patterns and looked down to learn Earth's forms.

sentences.zh: 」天文之事，其來已久。

translations.literal: 」Matters of astronomy have a history stretching far back.
translations.idiomatic: 」The study of heaven goes back a very long way.

sentences.zh: 太祖革命受終，膺集期運。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor received the mandate through revolution and accepted the transfer of the throne, taking upon himself the destined fortune of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor rose by revolution and received the transfer of power, he grasped the fortune of the age.

sentences.zh: 宋昇明三年，太史令將作匠文孝建陳天文，奏曰：「自孝建元年至昇明三年，日蝕有十，虧上有七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming of Song, Wen Xiaojian, Director of Astronomy and Master of Works, presented a report on celestial phenomena and memorialized: 「From the first year of Xiaojian to the third year of Shengming, solar eclipses numbered ten, with upper obscuration in seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's third Shengming year, Wen Xiaojian—Director of Astronomy and Master of Works—reported celestial omens and memorialized: 「From Xiaojian 1 through Shengming 3 there were ten solar eclipses, seven with the sun obscured at the top.

sentences.zh: 占曰『有亡國失君之象』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『there is an image of a perished state and a lost ruler』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen-reading says, 『This points to a ruined kingdom and a fallen ruler.』

sentences.zh: 一曰『國命絕，主危亡』。

translations.literal: One reading says 『the state's mandate is cut off; the ruler faces peril and extinction』.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss reads, 『The dynastic line is broken; the sovereign is in mortal danger.』

sentences.zh: 孝建元年至昇明三年，太白經天五。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xiaojian to the third year of Shengming, Venus crossed heaven five times.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaojian 1 to Shengming 3, Venus crossed the meridian in daylight five times.

sentences.zh: 占曰『天下革，民更王，異姓興』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the realm is transformed; the people change their king; another surname rises』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『The realm will be overturned, the people will change kings, and a new house will rise.』

sentences.zh: 孝建元年至昇明三年，月犯房心四，太白犯房心五。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xiaojian to the third year of Shengming, the Moon transgressed Fang and Xin four times; Venus transgressed Fang and Xin five times.
translations.idiomatic: In the same span the Moon infringed on the Room and Heart mansions four times and Venus did so five times.

sentences.zh: 占曰『其國有喪，宋當之』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『that state will have mourning; Song will bear it』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says, 『The realm will mourn—and Song will be the one.』

sentences.zh: 孝建元年至永光元年，奔星出入紫宮有四。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xiaojian to the first year of Yongguang, shooting stars entering and leaving the Purple Palace numbered four.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaojian 1 through Yongguang 1, four shooting stars appeared entering and leaving the Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰『國去其君，有空國徙王』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the state loses its ruler; there is an empty state and a relocated king』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『The kingdom loses its lord; the throne sits empty and a ruler is driven abroad.』

sentences.zh: 大明二年至元徽四年，天再裂。

translations.literal: From the second year of Daming to the fourth year of Yuanhui, Heaven split twice.
translations.idiomatic: From Daming 2 through Yuanhui 4, the sky appeared to split twice.

sentences.zh: 占曰『陽不足，白虹貫日，人君惡之』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『yang is insufficient; a white rainbow pierces the sun; the ruler is ill-omened』.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss runs, 『Yang is insufficient—a white rainbow pierces the sun—and the sovereign is marked for misfortune.』

sentences.zh: 孝建二年至大明五年，月入太微。

translations.literal: From the second year of Xiaojian to the fifth year of Daming, the Moon entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaojian 2 to Daming 5, the Moon entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年至昇明三年，月又入太微。

translations.literal: From the first year of Taiyu to the third year of Shengming, the Moon again entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: From Taiyu 1 through Shengming 3, the Moon entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure again.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年至元徽二年，太白入太微各八，熒惑入太微六。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xiaojian to the second year of Yuanhui, Venus entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure eight times; Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure six times.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaojian 1 to Yuanhui 2, Venus entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure eight times and Mars did so six times.

sentences.zh: 占曰『七耀行不軌道，危亡之象。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the seven luminaries move off their proper paths—a sign of peril and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reads, 『The seven luminaries leave their proper courses—a sign of ruin and death.

sentences.zh: 貴人失權勢，主亦衰，當有王入爲主』。

translations.literal: Nobles lose power and rank; the ruler also declines; a king will enter and become master』.
translations.idiomatic: The great lose their standing, the sovereign weakens, and a new king will rise to rule』.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年至昇明二年，太白熒惑經羽林各三。

translations.literal: From the second year of Xiaojian to the second year of Shengming, Venus and Mars each passed through the Feathered Forest three times.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaojian 2 to Shengming 2, Venus and Mars each crossed the Feathered Forest asterism three times.

sentences.zh: 占曰『國殘更世』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the state is maimed and the age changes』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『The kingdom is broken and the dynasty turns over.』

sentences.zh: 孝建二年四月十三日，熒惑守南斗，成勾己。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the fourth month of the second year of Xiaojian, Mars stationed at the Southern Dipper, forming a gouji hook.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiaojian 2, fourth month, day 13, Mars held the Southern Dipper and formed a gouji hook configuration.

sentences.zh: 占曰『天下易正更元』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the realm changes its orthodoxy and begins a new era』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says, 『The realm will change its ruling house and inaugurate a new reign era.』

sentences.zh: 孝建三年十二月一日，填星熒惑辰星合于南斗。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month of the third year of Xiaojian, Saturn, Mars, and Mercury conjoined at the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiaojian 3, twelfth month, day 1, Saturn, Mars, and Mercury gathered in the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰『改立王公』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『princes and dukes are deposed and established anew』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『Princes and dukes will be removed and replaced.』

sentences.zh: 大明二年十二月二十六日，太白犯填星于斗。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month of the second year of Daming, Venus transgressed Saturn in the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On Daming 2, twelfth month, day 26, Venus infringed on Saturn in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月十五日，太白填星合于危。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the eleventh month of the sixth year, Venus and Saturn conjoined in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On year 6, eleventh month, day 15, Venus and Saturn gathered in the Wei mansion.

sentences.zh: 占曰『天子失土』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the Son of Heaven loses his territory』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says, 『The Son of Heaven will lose his lands.』

sentences.zh: 景和元年十月八日，熒惑守太微，成勾己。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the tenth month of the first year of Jinghe, Mars stationed at the Supreme Palace Enclosure, forming a gouji hook.
translations.idiomatic: On Jinghe 1, tenth month, day 8, Mars held the Supreme Palace Enclosure and formed a gouji hook configuration.

sentences.zh: 占曰『王者惡之，主命無期，有徙主，若主王，天下更紀』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『kings find it ominous; the ruler's lifespan is uncertain; there is a displaced sovereign; perhaps one becomes lord-king; the realm changes its era reckoning』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading runs, 『Kings take it as ill-omened; the sovereign's life is unbounded; a ruler is displaced; one may become king in his stead; the realm changes its dynastic reckoning.』

sentences.zh: 泰始三年正月十七日，白氣見西南，東西半天，名曰長庚。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the first month of the third year of Taishi, white vapor appeared in the southwest, spanning half the sky east to west; it was called Changgeng.
translations.idiomatic: On Taishi 3, first month, day 17, white vapor showed in the southwest, stretching east to west across half the sky; it was named Changgeng.

sentences.zh: 六年九月二十七日，白氣又見東南長二丈，竝形狀長大，猛過彗星。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month of the sixth year, white vapor appeared again in the southeast, two zhang long; both in shape were large and long, surpassing a comet in fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: On year 6, ninth month, day 27, white vapor appeared again in the southeast, two zhang in length; both were large and long in form, fiercer than a comet.

sentences.zh: 占曰『除舊布新易主之象，遠期一紀』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『an image of removing the old and spreading the new—changing masters; the distant term is one cycle』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says, 『A sign of sweeping out the old and raising the new—a change of master; the distant term is one twelve-year cycle.』

sentences.zh: 至昇明三年，一紀訖。

translations.literal: By the third year of Shengming, one cycle was complete.
translations.idiomatic: By Shengming 3, the twelve-year cycle had run its course.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年四月二十四日，太白犯填星于胃。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month of the fourth year of Taishi, Venus transgressed Saturn in Stomach.
translations.idiomatic: On Taishi 4, fourth month, day 24, Venus infringed on Saturn in the Stomach mansion.

sentences.zh: 占曰『主命惡之』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the ruler's lifespan is ill-omened』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『The sovereign's life is marked for misfortune.』

sentences.zh: 泰始七年六月十七日，太白歲星填星合于東井。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Taishi, Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn conjoined at the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On Taishi 7, sixth month, day 17, Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn gathered in the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 占曰『改立王公』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『princes and dukes are deposed and established anew』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says, 『Princes and dukes will be removed and replaced.』

sentences.zh: 元徽四年至昇明二年三月，日有頻食。

translations.literal: From the fourth year of Yuanhui to the third month of the second year of Shengming, the sun had frequent eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanhui 4 through the third month of Shengming 2, solar eclipses came in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 占曰『社稷將亡，王者惡之』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『the altars of state are about to perish; kings find it ominous』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『The altars of state face ruin—and kings take it as ill-omened.』

sentences.zh: 元徽四年十月十日，填星守太微宮，逆從行，歷四年。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the tenth month of the fourth year of Yuanhui, Saturn stationed at the Supreme Palace Enclosure, moving in reverse and direct motion, lasting four years.
translations.idiomatic: On Yuanhui 4, tenth month, day 10, Saturn held the Supreme Palace Enclosure, moving retrograde and direct for four years.

sentences.zh: 占曰『有亡君之戒，易世立王』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『there is a warning of a perished ruler; the age changes and a king is established』.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says, 『There is warning of a fallen sovereign; the age turns and a new king is raised.』

sentences.zh: 元徽五年七月一日，熒惑太白辰星合于翼。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, Mars, Venus, and Mercury conjoined in Wings.
translations.idiomatic: On Yuanhui 5, seventh month, day 1, Mars, Venus, and Mercury gathered in the Wings mansion.

sentences.zh: 占曰『改立王公』。

translations.literal: Prognostication says 『princes and dukes are deposed and established anew』.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is, 『Princes and dukes will be removed and replaced.』

sentences.zh: 昇明二年六月二十日，歲星守斗建。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the sixth month of the second year of Shengming, Jupiter stationed at Dipper Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: On Shengming 2, sixth month, day 20, Jupiter held Dipper Establishment.

sentences.zh: 陰陽終始之門，大赦昇平之所起，律歷七政之本源，德星守之，天下更年，五禮更興，多暴貴者。

translations.literal: The gate of yin-yang's end and beginning; where great amnesties and the ascension to peace arise; the root source of pitch pipes, calendars, and the seven regulators; when the Virtue Star holds it, the realm changes its year-count, the five rites are renewed, and many rise swiftly to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper Establishment is the gate where yin and yang turn over, where great amnesties and the rise of peace begin, and the root of pitch pipes, calendrics, and the seven luminaries; when the Virtue Star holds it, the realm changes its year-reckoning, the five rites are revived, and many are suddenly ennobled.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年十月一日，熒惑守輿鬼。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month of the second year of Shengming, Mars stationed at Chariot and Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: On Shengming 2, tenth month, day 1, Mars held the Chariot-and-Ghost asterism.

sentences.zh: 三年正月七日，熒惑守兩戒閒，成勾己。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the third year, Mars stationed between the two celestial boundaries, forming a gouji hook.
translations.idiomatic: On year 3, first month, day 7, Mars held position between the two ecliptic boundaries and formed a gouji hook configuration.

sentences.zh: 占曰『尊者失朝，必有亡國去王』。

translations.literal: Prognostication reads: "The exalted will lose court; there will surely be a perished state and a departed king."
translations.idiomatic: The omen reads: "The great will fall from court; a state will perish and its king be lost."

sentences.zh: 昇明三年正月十八日，辰星孟效西方。

translations.literal: Shengming year 3, first month, eighteenth day: Mercury made its first prominent appearance in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming 3, first month, eighteenth day: Mercury first appeared brightly in the west.

sentences.zh: 占曰『天下更王』。

translations.literal: Prognostication reads: "The realm will change its king."
translations.idiomatic: The omen reads: "The realm will change its king."

sentences.zh: 昇明三年四月，歲星在虛危，徘徊玄枵之野，則齊國有福厚，爲受慶之符。

translations.literal: Shengming year 3, fourth month: Jupiter was in Xu and Wei, lingering in the wilderness of Xuanxiao—thus Qi would enjoy deep blessing, a sign of receiving felicitation.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming 3, fourth month: Jupiter stood in Xu and Wei, circling the Xuanxiao quarter—an omen that Qi would receive great fortune and abundant blessing.

sentences.zh: 」今所記三辰七曜之變，起建元訖于隆昌，以續宋史。

translations.literal: "What is now recorded of the changes of the three luminaries and seven regulators begins at Jianyuan and runs to Longchang, continuing the Song History.
translations.idiomatic: "The celestial changes recorded below run from Jianyuan through Longchang, continuing the Song History.

sentences.zh: 建武世太史奏事，明帝不欲使天變外傳，竝祕而不出，自此闕焉。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era the Grand Astrologer's reports—Emperor Ming, not wishing heavenly anomalies to be spread abroad, kept them all secret and unpublished; hence the gap from that point.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwu the court astrologer's reports were suppressed: Emperor Ming would not let heavenly portents leak out, and from then on the record breaks off.

sentences.zh: 建元二年九月甲午朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 2, ninth month, jiawu new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 2, ninth month, jiawu new moon: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 三年七月己未朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: Year 3, seventh month, jiwei new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3, seventh month, jiwei new moon: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 永明元年十二月乙巳朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: Yongming year 1, twelfth month, yisi new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 1, twelfth month, yisi new moon: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月癸未朔，加時在午之半度，到未初見日始蝕，虧起西北角，蝕十分之四，申時光色復還。

translations.literal: Year 10, twelfth month, guiwei new moon: the appointed hour was at half a degree into wu; reaching the start of wei the sun began to be eclipsed; the bite began at the northwest corner; four-tenths was eclipsed; at shen hour light and color were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10, twelfth month, guiwei new moon: the eclipse fell at mid-wu; as wei began the sun first darkened from the northwest; four-tenths of the disk was covered; by shen hour full light returned.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年五月甲戌合朔，巳時日蝕三分之一，午時光復還。

translations.literal: Longchang year 1, fifth month, jiaxu conjunction at new moon: at si hour the sun was one-third eclipsed; at wu hour light was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang 1, fifth month, jiaxu new moon: at si hour one-third of the sun was eclipsed; by wu hour light had returned.

sentences.zh: 建元四年七月戊辰，月在危宿蝕。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 4, seventh month, wuchen: the moon was eclipsed in the Wei asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 4, seventh month, wuchen: the moon was eclipsed in the Wei asterism.

sentences.zh: 永明二年四月丁巳，月在南斗宿蝕。

translations.literal: Yongming year 2, fourth month, dingsi: the moon was eclipsed in the Southern Dipper asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 2, fourth month, dingsi: the moon was eclipsed in the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月戊寅，月入東井曠中，因蝕三分之一。

translations.literal: Year 3, eleventh month, wuyin: the moon entered the open space of the Eastern Well and was eclipsed one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3, eleventh month, wuyin: the moon entered the open field of the Eastern Well and was one-third eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 五年三月庚子，月在氐宿蝕。

translations.literal: Year 5, third month, gengzi: the moon was eclipsed in the Di asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, third month, gengzi: the moon was eclipsed in the Di asterism.

sentences.zh: 九月戊戌，月在胃宿蝕。

translations.literal: Ninth month, wuxu: the moon was eclipsed in the Stomach asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wuxu: the moon was eclipsed in the Stomach asterism.

sentences.zh: 六年九月癸巳，月蝕在婁宿九度，加時在寅之少弱，虧起東北角，蝕十五分之十一。

translations.literal: Year 6, ninth month, guisi: lunar eclipse at the ninth degree of the Lou asterism; timed at slight weakness into yin; the bite began at the northeast corner; eleven-fifteenths was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6, ninth month, guisi: the moon was eclipsed at the ninth degree of Lou; the shadow began at the northeast when yin was barely past; eleven-fifteenths of the disk was covered.

sentences.zh: 十五日子時，蝕從東北始，至子時末都旣，到丑時光色還復。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth, at zi hour the eclipse began from the northeast; by the end of zi it was wholly complete; by chou hour light and color were restored.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth, at zi hour the shadow started in the northeast; by the end of zi the eclipse was total; by chou hour the moon's light had returned.

sentences.zh: 七年八月丁亥，月在奎宿蝕。

translations.literal: Year 7, eighth month, dinghai: the moon was eclipsed in the Kui asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7, eighth month, dinghai: the moon was eclipsed in the Kui asterism.

sentences.zh: 十月庚辰，月奄蝕熒惑。

translations.literal: Tenth month, gengchen: the moon covered and eclipsed Mars.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, gengchen: the moon occulted Mars.

sentences.zh: 八年六月庚寅，月奄蝕畢左股第一星。

translations.literal: Year 8, sixth month, gengyin: the moon covered and eclipsed the first star of the left thigh of Net.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8, sixth month, gengyin: the moon occulted the first star of the left thigh of the Net asterism.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月丁酉，月蝕在柳度，加時在酉之少弱，到亥時月蝕起東角七分之二，至子時光色還復。

translations.literal: Year 10, twelfth month, dingyou: lunar eclipse at the Willow degree; timed at slight weakness into you; reaching hai hour the eclipse began at two-sevenths from the east edge; by zi hour light and color were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10, twelfth month, dingyou: the moon was eclipsed in Willow; the shadow began at you when the hour was barely past; at hai hour two-sevenths of the eastern rim was eaten; by zi hour the light had returned.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年四月癸亥，月蝕，色赤如血。

translations.literal: Yongtai year 1, fourth month, guihai: lunar eclipse; the color was red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai 1, fourth month, guihai: the moon was eclipsed, its color red as blood.

sentences.zh: 三日而大司馬王敬則舉兵，衆以爲敬則祲烈所感。

translations.literal: Three days later Grand Marshal Wang Jingze raised troops; the multitude held that Jingze had been moved by these ominous fierce portents.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Grand Marshal Wang Jingze rose in rebellion; many took it as a response to these violent omens.

sentences.zh: 永元元年八月己未，月蝕盡，色皆赤。

translations.literal: Yongyuan year 1, eighth month, jiwei: the moon was wholly eclipsed; the color was all red.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 1, eighth month, jiwei: the moon was totally eclipsed, glowing wholly red.

sentences.zh: 是夜，始安王遙光伏誅。

translations.literal: That night Prince of Shian Xiao Yaoguang was executed.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Prince of Shian Xiao Yaoguang was put to death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：日月代照，實重天行。

translations.literal: The historians say: Sun and moon alternate in shining—this truly weighs on the celestial motion.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler remarks: Sun and moon take turns in giving light—a matter of grave importance in heaven's cycles.

sentences.zh: 上交下蝕，同度相掩。

translations.literal: Upper node, lower eclipse; same degree, mutually covering.
translations.idiomatic: The node lies above and the eclipse below; at the same degree they cover one another.

sentences.zh: 案舊說曰「日有五蝕」，謂起上下左右中央是也。

translations.literal: Examining the old doctrine: "The sun has five eclipses"—meaning starting from top, bottom, left, right, and center.
translations.idiomatic: The old teaching holds that "the sun has five kinds of eclipse"—beginning from above, below, left, right, and the center.

sentences.zh: 交會舊術，日蝕不從東始，以月從其西，東行及日。

translations.literal: The old method of node conjunction: solar eclipses do not begin from the east, for the moon comes from the west, travels east, and reaches the sun.
translations.idiomatic: By the old conjunction method, a solar eclipse never starts in the east: the moon approaches from the west, moves eastward, and meets the sun.

sentences.zh: 於交中，交從外入內者，先會後交，虧西南角；

translations.literal: At the node, when the node enters from outside: encounter first then node-crossing, bite at the southwest corner;
translations.idiomatic: At conjunction, if the node enters from without: first encounter then crossing, and the shadow bites the southwest corner;

sentences.zh: 先交後會，虧西北角；

translations.literal: node-crossing first then encounter, bite at the northwest corner;
translations.idiomatic: crossing first then encounter, and the shadow bites the northwest corner;

sentences.zh: 交從內出者，先會後交，虧西北角；

translations.literal: when the node exits from inside: encounter first then node-crossing, bite at the northwest corner;
translations.idiomatic: if the node exits from within: first encounter then crossing, and the shadow bites the northwest corner;

sentences.zh: 先交後會，虧西南角。

translations.literal: node-crossing first then encounter, bite at the southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: crossing first then encounter, and the shadow bites the southwest corner.

sentences.zh: 日正在交中者，則虧於西，故不嘗蝕東也。

translations.literal: When the sun is directly at the node, the bite is on the west—thus it never eclipses from the east.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun stands right at the node, the shadow falls on the west—so an eclipse never begins in the east.

sentences.zh: 若日中有虧，名爲黑子，不名爲蝕也。

translations.literal: If there is a bite within the sun, it is called a black spot—not called an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: A blemish within the sun itself is called a black spot, not an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 漢尚書令黃香曰：「日蝕皆從西，月蝕皆從東，無上下中央者。

translations.literal: Han Director of the Masters of Writing Huang Xiang said: "Solar eclipses all begin from the west; lunar eclipses all begin from the east; there are none from top, bottom, or center.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xiang, Director of the Masters of Writing under Han, said: "Solar eclipses always start in the west and lunar eclipses in the east; none begin from above, below, or the center.

sentences.zh: 」《春秋》魯桓三年日蝕，貫中下上竟黑。

translations.literal: "The Spring and Autumn Annals: Lu Huan year 3 solar eclipse—pierced middle, top and bottom, all turned black.
translations.idiomatic: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records a solar eclipse in Duke Huan of Lu's third year that cut through the center and left top and bottom wholly black.

sentences.zh: 疑者以爲日月正等，月何得小而見日中。

translations.literal: Doubters held that sun and moon are equal in size—how could the moon be small yet be seen within the sun?
translations.idiomatic: Skeptics argued that if sun and moon are the same size, how could the smaller moon appear inside the sun?

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「月正掩日，日光從四邊出，故言從中起也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "The moon was directly covering the sun; sunlight issued from all four sides—hence it is said to begin from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan replied: "The moon was directly masking the sun, and light streamed out on every side—hence the report that the eclipse began at the center.

sentences.zh: 」王逸以爲「月若掩日，當蝕日西，月行旣疾，須臾應過西崖旣，復次食東崖，今察日蝕西崖缺，而光已復過東崖而獨不掩」。

translations.literal: "Wang Yi held: "If the moon covered the sun, it should eclipse the sun's west; the moon moves swiftly and in an instant should have passed the western rim, then again eaten the eastern rim—yet now we observe the sun's western rim is eaten, while light has already passed the eastern rim and that alone is not covered."
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Yi objected: "If the moon masked the sun, it ought to eat the western edge first; moving quickly, it should soon pass the western limb and then bite the eastern one. Yet we see the western rim darkened while light has already returned past the eastern rim, which alone remains uncovered."

sentences.zh: 逸之此意，實爲巨疑。

translations.literal: Wang Yi's point here is truly a great doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi's objection raises a serious difficulty.

sentences.zh: 先儒難「月以望蝕，去日極遠，誰蝕月乎？

translations.literal: Earlier scholars objected: "The moon is eclipsed at full moon, extremely far from the sun—who eclipses the moon?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars asked: "The moon is eclipsed at full moon, when it is farthest from the sun—what could eclipse it?

sentences.zh: 」說者稱「日有暗氣，天有虛道，常與日衡相對，月行在虛道中，則爲氣所弇，故月爲蝕也。

translations.literal: "Respondents said: "The sun has dark qi; heaven has a void path constantly opposite the sun's axis; when the moon travels in the void path it is blotted by qi—thus the moon is eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: "Defenders answered: "The sun casts a dark vapor, and heaven has a void track always opposite the solar axis. When the moon passes through that track, the vapor covers it, and the moon is eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 雖時加夜半，日月當子午，正隔於地，猶爲暗氣所蝕，以天體大而地形小故也。

translations.literal: Even when timed at midnight, sun and moon at south and north zenith directly separated by earth, still eclipsed by dark qi—because the heavenly body is large and the terrestrial form small.
translations.idiomatic: Even at midnight, when sun and moon stand at south and north and the earth lies directly between them, the dark vapor can still eclipse the moon, because the heavens are vast and the earth small.

sentences.zh: 暗虛之氣，如以鏡在日下，其光耀魄，乃見於陰中，常與日衡相對，故當星星亡，當月月蝕」。

translations.literal: The dark void qi is like holding a mirror under the sun—its light shines the brightness and is seen in shadow, constantly opposite the sun's axis—hence when a star [passes it] the star vanishes, when the moon [passes it] the moon is eclipsed."
translations.idiomatic: That dark void is like a mirror held beneath the sun: its reflected light shows in the shadow and always faces the solar axis. Hence when a star crosses it the star disappears, and when the moon crosses it the moon is eclipsed."

sentences.zh: 今問之曰：「星月同體，俱兆日耀，當月之蝕，星不必亡。

translations.literal: Now one asks: "Stars and moon are the same kind of body, both reflecting solar glory—when the moon is eclipsed, stars need not vanish.
translations.idiomatic: One may still ask: "Stars and moon alike reflect the sun's light—when the moon is eclipsed, why need stars not vanish too?

sentences.zh: 若更有所當，星未嘗蝕，同稟異虧，其故何也？

translations.literal: If there were another [body] it encountered, stars are never eclipsed—same endowment but different waning—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: If something else were blocking the path, stars are never eclipsed; they share the same light yet suffer differently—why?

sentences.zh: 」荅曰：「月爲陰主，以當陽位，體敵勢交，自招盈損。

translations.literal: "Answer: "The moon is mistress of yin, standing in the yang position—bodies matched, forces in interplay, it naturally invites waxing and waning.
translations.idiomatic: "The reply: "The moon is yin's sovereign standing in yang's place; matched in body and crossed in force, it naturally waxes and wanes.

sentences.zh: 星雖同類，而精景陋狹，小毀皆亡，無有受蝕之地，纖光可滿，亦不與弦望同形。

translations.literal: Stars though of the same kind have narrow, cramped essences and light—slight damage and all vanish, with no ground to receive eclipse; their slender light can fill [the void], nor do they share the crescent and full forms."
translations.idiomatic: Stars, though akin, have small and narrow bodies and light; the least harm extinguishes them, and they have no place to be eclipsed. Their thin light can fill the void, and they do not share the moon's crescent and full shapes."

sentences.zh: 」又難曰：「日之夜蝕，驗於夜星之亡，晝蝕旣盡，晝星何故反不見？

translations.literal: Another objection was raised: "When the sun is eclipsed at night, this is verified by the disappearance of stars at night; when a daytime eclipse is complete, why are daytime stars not seen in turn?"
translations.idiomatic: Another objection was raised: "Night solar eclipses are confirmed when stars vanish at night—yet when a daytime eclipse is total, why do daytime stars not appear?"

sentences.zh: 」答之曰：「夫言光有所衝，則有不衝之光矣；

translations.literal: The answer was: "When one says light has something it strikes against, there is also light that does not strike;"
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "If light sometimes strikes something, it also sometimes does not;"

sentences.zh: 言有所當，亦有所不當矣。

translations.literal: when one says something is aligned, there is also what is not aligned."
translations.idiomatic: if something is sometimes aligned, it is also sometimes not aligned."

sentences.zh: 夜食度遠，與所當而同沒；

translations.literal: At a night eclipse the degree is far, and it sets together with what is aligned;
translations.idiomatic: At a night eclipse the position is far off, and it sets together with what is aligned;

sentences.zh: 晝食度近，由非衝而得明。

translations.literal: at a day eclipse the degree is near, and brightness comes from not striking directly."
translations.idiomatic: at a day eclipse the position is near, and light returns because there is no direct strike."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「太白經天，實緣遠日。

translations.literal: Another question: "When Venus crosses the heavens, it is truly because it is far from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Another question: "Venus crossing the sky truly comes from standing far from the sun.

sentences.zh: 今度近更明，於何取喻？

translations.literal: Now at a near degree it shines brighter—what analogy does one take?"
translations.idiomatic: Now at a nearer position it shines even brighter—what comparison fits?"

sentences.zh: 」荅曰：「向論二蝕之體，周衝不同，經與不經，自由星遲疾，難蝕引經，恐未得也。」

translations.literal: The answer: "The discussion just now of the two forms of eclipse differed in orbital alignment; whether one crosses the sky or not depends freely on whether the star is slow or fast. To cite crossing the sky in explaining eclipses is probably not valid."
translations.idiomatic: The reply: "The two eclipse forms just discussed differ in how their circuits align; whether a star crosses the sky depends on its speed. Invoking sky-crossing to explain eclipses probably will not do."

sentences.zh: 日光色

translations.literal: Color of sunlight
translations.idiomatic: Solar Color

sentences.zh: 建元四年十一月午時，日色赤黃無光，至暮，在箕宿。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 4, eleventh month, at the noon hour—the sun was reddish-yellow and without brilliance until evening, in the Winnowing-Basket mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Jianyuan 4, at noon the sun turned reddish yellow and lost its light until evening, in the Winnowing-Basket mansion.

sentences.zh: 二年閏正月乙酉，日黃赤無光，至暮。

translations.literal: Second year, intercalary first month, on yiyou—the sun was yellow-red and without brilliance until evening.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of year 2, on yiyou, the sun was yellow-red and dim until evening.

sentences.zh: 永明五年十一月丁亥，日出高三竿，失色赤黃，日暈，虹抱珥直背。

translations.literal: Yongming year 5, eleventh month, on dinghai—at sunrise three bamboo-poles high the sun lost its color to red-yellow, showed a solar halo, with rainbow, embrace, spikes, straight streak, and counter-glow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yongming 5, on dinghai, when the sun stood three bamboo poles above the horizon it faded red-yellow, showed a solar halo, and bore rainbow, embrace, spikes, straight streak, and counter-glow.

sentences.zh: 建元元年十二月未時，日暈，帀，黃白色，至申乃消散。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 1, twelfth month, at the wei hour—a solar halo, complete ring, yellow-white, dissipated by the shen hour.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Jianyuan 1, at the wei hour the sun showed a complete yellow-white halo that cleared by the shen hour.

sentences.zh: 永明二年正月丁酉，日交暈再重。

translations.literal: Yongming year 2, first month, on dingyou—double intersecting solar halos, layered twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongming 2, on dingyou, the sun showed double intersecting halos.

sentences.zh: 三年二月丁卯，日有半暈，暈上生一闕。

translations.literal: Year 3, second month, on dingmao—the sun had a half-halo, and on the halo a gap formed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 3, on dingmao, the sun bore a half-halo with a break in the ring.

sentences.zh: 四年五月丙午，日暈再重，仍白虹貫日，在東井度。

translations.literal: Year 4, fifth month, on bingwu—double solar halos, and a white arc pierced the sun, in the Well mansion degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 4, on bingwu, double solar halos appeared and a white arc cut across the sun in the Well mansion.

sentences.zh: 六年三月甲申，日於蘭雲中薄半暈，須臾過帀，日東南暈外有一直，竝黃色。

translations.literal: Year 6, third month, on jiashen—the sun amid orchid-colored clouds showed a faint half-halo; presently it passed into full ring; southeast of the halo outside the sun a straight streak, all yellow.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 6, on jiashen, the sun in orchid-tinted clouds showed a thin half-halo, then quickly a full ring; southeast outside the halo a straight yellow streak appeared.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，日暈，須臾，日西北生虹貫日中。

translations.literal: On renchen—a solar halo; presently from the northwest a white arc pierced through the sun's center.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen a solar halo formed; presently a white arc from the northwest pierced the sun's center.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月己亥，日半暈，南面不帀，日東西帶暈，各生珥，長三尺，白色，珥各長十丈許，正衝日，久久消散，背因成重暈，竝青絳色。

translations.literal: Year 8, eleventh month, on jihai—half solar halo, the south side not complete; east and west band-halos each bore spikes three chi long, white; each spike about ten zhang, directly facing the sun; after long time dissipated; counter-glow then formed double halos, all bluish and purplish.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 8, on jihai, a half-halo left the south incomplete; east and west band-halos each grew white three-chi spikes about ten zhang long, facing the sun; after long delay all faded, and counter-glow formed double halos in blue and purple.

sentences.zh: 九年正月甲午，日半暈，南面不帀，北帶暈生一抱，東西各生一珥，抱北又有半暈，抱珥竝黃色，北又生白虹貫日，久久消散。

translations.literal: Year 9, first month, on jiawu—half halo, south incomplete; on the north band-halo an embrace formed; east and west each a spike; north of the embrace another half-halo; embrace and spikes all yellow; north again a white arc pierced the sun; after long time dissipated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 9, on jiawu, a half-halo left the south open; the north band-halo grew an embrace, east and west each a spike, and north of the embrace another half-halo—all yellow; north again a white arc pierced the sun, then slowly cleared.

sentences.zh: 建元元年六月甲申，日南北兩珥，西有抱，黃白色。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 1, sixth month, on jiashen—two spikes south and north on the sun, an embrace on the west, yellow-white.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jianyuan 1, on jiashen, the sun bore two yellow-white spikes north and south and an embrace on the west.

sentences.zh: 永明二年十一月辛巳，日東北有一背。

translations.literal: Yongming year 2, eleventh month, on xinsi—a counter-glow northeast of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yongming 2, on xinsi, a counter-glow appeared northeast of the sun.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月庚寅，日西北有一背。

translations.literal: Year 3, eleventh month, on gengyin—a counter-glow northwest of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 3, on gengyin, a counter-glow appeared northwest of the sun.

sentences.zh: 四年正月辛巳，日南北各生一珥，又生一背。

translations.literal: Year 4, first month, on xinsi—south and north each bore a spike, and a counter-glow also formed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 4, on xinsi, the sun grew a spike south and north and also a counter-glow.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛未，日西北生一直，黃白色。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on xinwei—a straight streak formed northwest of the sun, yellow-white.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinwei, a yellow-white straight streak formed northwest of the sun.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，日北生一背，青絳色。

translations.literal: On wuyin—a counter-glow formed north of the sun, bluish-purplish.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin a blue-purple counter-glow formed north of the sun.

sentences.zh: 五年八月己卯，日東南生一珥，竝青絳色。

translations.literal: Year 5, eighth month, on jimao—a spike formed southeast of the sun, also bluish-purplish.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 5, on jimao, a blue-purple spike formed southeast of the sun.

sentences.zh: 六年二月丁巳，日東北生黃色，北有一珥，黃赤色，久久竝散。

translations.literal: Year 6, second month, on dingsi—yellow color formed northeast of the sun; north a spike, yellow-red; after long time all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 6, on dingsi, yellow light appeared northeast of the sun; north a yellow-red spike; after long delay all dispersed.

sentences.zh: 庚申，日西有一背，赤青色，東西生一直，南北各生一珥，竝黃白色。

translations.literal: On gengshen—a counter-glow west of the sun, red-bluish; east and west a straight streak; south and north each a spike—all yellow-white.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen a red-blue counter-glow appeared west of the sun; east and west a straight streak; south and north each a yellow-white spike.

sentences.zh: 七年十月癸未，日東北生一背，青赤色，須臾消。

translations.literal: Year 7, tenth month, on guiwei—a counter-glow northeast of the sun, green-red, dissipated presently.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 7, on guiwei, a green-red counter-glow northeast of the sun quickly faded.

sentences.zh: 八年六月戊寅，日於蒼白雲中南北各生一珥，青黃絳雜色，澤潤，竝長三尺許，至巳午消。

translations.literal: Year 8, sixth month, on wuyin—the sun amid pale clouds bore a spike south and north, mixed green-yellow-purple, lustrous, each about three chi long; vanished by si and wu hours.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 8, on wuyin, the sun in pale clouds bore north and south spikes of mixed green, yellow, and purple, bright and about three chi long; they vanished by si and wu hours.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年正月壬戌，日於蘭雲中暈，南北帶暈各生一直，同長一丈，須臾消。

translations.literal: Longchang year 1, first month, on renxu—the sun amid orchid-colored clouds showed a halo; on the south and north band-halos each a straight streak, equally one zhang long; dissipated presently.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Longchang 1, on renxu, the sun in orchid-tinted clouds showed a halo; south and north band-halos each grew a one-zhang straight streak, then quickly cleared.

sentences.zh: 永元元年十二月乙酉，日中有三黑子。

translations.literal: Yongyuan year 1, twelfth month, on yiyou—three black spots in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yongyuan 1, on yiyou, three black spots appeared on the sun.

sentences.zh: 月暈犯

translations.literal: Lunar halo transits
translations.idiomatic: Lunar Halos and Transits

sentences.zh: 建元四年十月庚寅，月暈五車及參頭。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 4, tenth month, on gengyin—the moon's halo encompassed Wuche and Cantou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianyuan 4, on gengyin, the moon's halo ringed the Five Chariots and Cantou.

sentences.zh: 永明元年正月壬辰，是日至十五日，月三暈太微及熒惑。

translations.literal: Yongming year 1, first month, on renchen—from this day to the fifteenth, the moon thrice haloed Taiwei and Yinghuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongming 1, on renchen, from that day through the fifteenth the moon thrice haloed Taiwei and Mars.

sentences.zh: 三月庚申至十三日，月三暈太微及熒惑。

translations.literal: Third month, from gengshen to the thirteenth, the moon thrice haloed Taiwei and Yinghuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, from gengshen through the thirteenth, the moon thrice haloed Taiwei and Mars.

sentences.zh: 五年二月乙未，自九日至是日，月三暈太微。

translations.literal: Year 5, second month, on yiwei—from the ninth to this day, the moon thrice haloed Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 5, on yiwei, from the ninth through that day the moon thrice haloed Taiwei.

sentences.zh: 六年二月壬戌甲夜、十三日甲夜、十五日甲夜，月竝暈太微。

translations.literal: Year 6, second month—on nights of renchen-jia, the thirteenth jia night, and the fifteenth jia night, the moon all showed halos encompassing Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 6, on the renchen jia watch, the thirteenth jia watch, and the fifteenth jia watch, the moon each time haloed Taiwei.

sentences.zh: 永明元年十一月己未，月南北各生一珥，又有一抱。

translations.literal: Yongming year 1, eleventh month, on jiwei—the moon bore a spike south and north, and also an embrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yongming 1, on jiwei, the moon grew spikes south and north and also an embrace.

sentences.zh: 月犯列星

translations.literal: Lunar transits of listed stars
translations.idiomatic: Lunar Transits of Individual Stars

sentences.zh: 建元元年七月丁未，月犯心大星北一寸。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 1, seventh month, on dingwei—the moon transited the great star of Heart, one cun north.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jianyuan 1, on dingwei, the moon transited the great star of Heart one cun to the north.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，月入軒轅中犯第二星。

translations.literal: On dingmao—the moon entered Xuanyuan and transited the second star.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the moon entered Xuanyuan and transited the second star.

sentences.zh: 十月丙申，月在心大星西北七寸。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on bingshen—the moon was northwest of the great star of Heart by seven cun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on bingshen, the moon stood seven cun northwest of the great star of Heart.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬戌，月在氐東南星五寸。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renxu—the moon was five cun from Di's southeastern star.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renxu, the moon stood five cun from Di's southeastern star.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，月犯太微西蕃南頭第一星。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on yiyou—the moon transited the first star at the southern end of Taiwei's western rampart.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, the moon transited the first star at the south end of Taiwei's western rampart.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，月行房道中，無所犯。

translations.literal: On gengyin—the moon traveled in the Road of Room, transiting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the moon passed along the Road of Room without transiting any star.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，月入南斗魁中，無所犯。

sentences.zh: 甲辰，月行入氐中，掩犯東北星。

translations.literal: On jiachen—the moon traveled into Root, occulting and encroaching upon the northeastern star.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the moon entered Root and occulted and encroached upon the northeastern star.

sentences.zh: 壬子，月行入羽林。

translations.literal: On renzi—the moon traveled into the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the moon entered the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 三月己卯，月行入羽林，在填星東北七寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Third month, on jimao—the moon traveled into the Feathered Forest, northeast of Saturn by seven cun, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jimao, the moon entered the Feathered Forest seven cun northeast of Saturn, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 在危四度。

translations.literal: In the fourth degree of Rooftop.
translations.idiomatic: It stood in the fourth degree of Rooftop.

sentences.zh: 四月甲午，月行入太微，在右掖門內。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on jiawu—the moon traveled into Taiwei, inside the Right Flank Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jiawu, the moon entered Taiwei inside the Right Flank Gate.

sentences.zh: 丙午，月行在危度，入羽林。

translations.literal: On bingwu—the moon traveled at the Rooftop degree, entering the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the moon stood at the Rooftop degree and entered the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，月掩南斗第三星。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jisi—the moon occulted the third star of the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jisi, the moon occulted the third star of the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，月行在危度，入羽林。

translations.literal: On jiaxu—the moon traveled at the Rooftop degree, entering the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the moon stood at the Rooftop degree and entered the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，月在張度，在熒惑星東三寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on wuzi—the moon stood at the Extended Net degree, three cun east of Mars, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi, the moon stood at the Extended Net degree three cun east of Mars, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 己丑，月行入太微，在右掖門。

translations.literal: On jichou—the moon traveled into Taiwei, at the Right Flank Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the moon entered Taiwei at the Right Flank Gate.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，月掩西建星西。

translations.literal: On dingyou—the moon occulted the west star of Western Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the moon occulted Western Establishment's west star.

sentences.zh: 丁未，月行入畢，犯右股大赤星。

translations.literal: On dingwei—the moon traveled into Net, encroaching upon the great red star of the right thigh.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the moon entered Net and encroached upon the right-thigh great red star.

sentences.zh: 七月甲戌，月行在畢躔星西北六寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on jiaxu—the moon traveled six cun northwest of Net's station star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jiaxu, the moon stood six cun northwest of Net's station star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，月在東井北轅東頭第二星西南九寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On dingchou—the moon stood nine cun southwest of the second star at the eastern end of the Eastern Well's northern crossbar, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the moon stood nine cun southwest of the second star at the eastern end of the Eastern Well's northern crossbar, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 八月辛卯，月行西建星東一尺，又在東星西四寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on xinmao—the moon traveled one chi east of Western Establishment star, and also four cun west of the east star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao, the moon stood one chi east of Western Establishment star and four cun west of its east star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，月行在畢右股大赤星東北四寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On renyin—the moon traveled four cun northeast of Net's right thigh great red star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the moon stood four cun northeast of Net's right-thigh great red star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，月行入東井曠中，無所犯。

translations.literal: On jiachen—the moon traveled into the Eastern Well open center, encroaching upon nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 戊申，月行在軒轅女主星西九寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On wushen—the moon traveled nine cun west of Xuanyuan's lady master star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the moon stood nine cun west of Xuanyuan's lady master star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，月入太微，在左執法星北二尺七寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On xinhai—the moon entered Taiwei, two chi seven cun north of the Left Law Administrator star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the moon entered Taiwei two chi seven cun north of the Left Law Administrator star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 九月癸亥，月行掩犯填星一寸，在危度。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on guihai—the moon traveled, occulting and encroaching upon Saturn by one cun, in the Rooftop degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guihai, the moon occulted and encroached upon Saturn by one cun in the Rooftop degree.

sentences.zh: 十月辛卯，月在危度，入羽林，無所犯。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on xinmao—the moon stood at the Rooftop degree, entering the Feathered Forest without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on xinmao, the moon stood at the Rooftop degree and entered the Feathered Forest without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，月入東井曠中，無所犯。

translations.literal: On guihai—the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子，月入畢，進右股大赤星西北五寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on jiazi—the moon entered Net, advancing to five cun northwest of the great red star of the right thigh, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, the moon entered Net and advanced to five cun northwest of the right-thigh great red star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 壬申，月入太微，在右執法星東北一尺三寸，無所犯。

translations.literal: On renshen—the moon entered Taiwei, one chi three cun northeast of the Right Law Administrator star, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the moon entered Taiwei one chi three cun northeast of the Right Law Administrator star without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，月入氐，無所犯。

translations.literal: On dingchou—the moon entered Root without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the moon entered Root without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲午，月入東井曠中，又進北轅東頭第二星四寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jiawu—the moon entered the Eastern Well open center, and also advanced to four cun from the second star at the eastern end of the northern crossbar, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, the moon entered the Eastern Well open center and advanced to four cun from the second star at the eastern end of the northern crossbar, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 庚子，月入太微，在右執法星東北三尺，無所犯。

translations.literal: On gengzi—the moon entered Taiwei, three chi northeast of the Right Law Administrator star, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the moon entered Taiwei three chi northeast of the Right Law Administrator star without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月辛酉，月入東井曠中，無所犯。

translations.literal: Year 11, first month, on xinyou—the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 11, on xinyou, the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，月在軒轅女主星北八寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On yichou—the moon stood eight cun north of Xuanyuan's lady master star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the moon stood eight cun north of Xuanyuan's lady master star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 壬申，月行在氐星東北九寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On renshen—the moon traveled nine cun northeast of the Root star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the moon stood nine cun northeast of the Root star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 二月甲午，月行入太微，在上將星東北一尺五寸，無所犯。

translations.literal: Second month, on jiawu—the moon traveled into Taiwei, one chi five cun northeast of the supreme general star, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiawu, the moon entered Taiwei one chi five cun northeast of the supreme general star without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，月行掩犯南斗第六星。

translations.literal: On renyin—the moon traveled, occulting and encroaching upon the sixth star of the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the moon occulted and encroached upon the sixth star of the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，月掩犯西建中星，又掩東星。

translations.literal: On guimao—the moon occulted and encroached upon Western Establishment's middle star, and also occulted the east star.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the moon occulted and encroached upon Western Establishment's middle star, and also occulted its east star.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑，月入太微，在右執法西北一尺四寸，無所犯。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on yichou—the moon entered Taiwei, one chi four cun northwest of the Right Law Administrator, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on yichou, the moon entered Taiwei one chi four cun northwest of the Right Law Administrator without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，月行在危度，入羽林，無所犯。

translations.literal: On renyin—the moon traveled at the Rooftop degree, entering the Feathered Forest without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the moon stood at the Rooftop degree and entered the Feathered Forest without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 五月丁巳，月行入太微左執法星北三尺，無所犯。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on dingsi—the moon traveled into Taiwei three chi north of the Left Law Administrator star, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi, the moon entered Taiwei three chi north of the Left Law Administrator star without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 甲子，月行在南斗第二星西七寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On jiazi—the moon traveled seven cun west of the second star of the Southern Dipper, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the moon stood seven cun west of the second star of the Southern Dipper, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，月掩犯西建中星。

translations.literal: On yichou—the moon occulted and encroached upon Western Establishment's middle star.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the moon occulted and encroached upon Western Establishment's middle star.

sentences.zh: 又犯東星六寸。

translations.literal: It also encroached upon the east star by six cun.
translations.idiomatic: It also encroached upon the east star by six cun.

sentences.zh: 六月辛丑，月行掩犯畢左股第三星。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on xinchou—the moon traveled, occulting and encroaching upon the third star of Net's left thigh.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinchou, the moon occulted and encroached upon the third star of Net's left thigh.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，月入畢。

translations.literal: On renyin—the moon entered Net.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the moon entered Net.

sentences.zh: 七月壬子，月入太微，在左執法東三尺，無所犯。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on renzi—the moon entered Taiwei, three chi east of the Left Law Administrator, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on renzi, the moon entered Taiwei three chi east of the Left Law Administrator without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，月行入氐，在東北星西南六寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On bingchen—the moon traveled into Root, six cun southwest of the northeastern star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the moon entered Root six cun southwest of the northeastern star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 己未，月行南斗第六星南四寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On jiwei—the moon traveled four cun south of the sixth star of the Southern Dipper, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the moon stood four cun south of the sixth star of the Southern Dipper, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 庚申，月行在西建星東南一寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On gengshen—the moon traveled one cun southeast of Western Establishment star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the moon stood one cun southeast of Western Establishment star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 九月庚寅，月行在哭星西南六寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: September, on gengyin—the moon traveled six cun southwest of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengyin, the moon stood six cun southwest of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，月行在營室度，入羽林，無所犯。

translations.literal: On renchen—the moon traveled at the Encampment degree, entering the Feathered Forest without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the moon stood at the Encampment degree and entered the Feathered Forest without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，月入畢，在右股大赤星西北六寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On dingyou—the moon entered Net, six cun northwest of the great red star of the right thigh, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the moon entered Net six cun northwest of the right-thigh great red star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 己亥，月入東井曠中，無所犯。

translations.literal: On jihai—the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the moon entered the Eastern Well open center without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，月行太微，當右掖門內，在屏星西南六寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On yisi—the moon traveled through Taiwei, inside the Right Flank Gate, six cun southwest of the Screen Star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the moon passed through Taiwei inside the Right Flank Gate six cun southwest of the Screen Star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 十月壬午，月行在東建中星九寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on renwu—the moon traveled nine cun from Eastern Establishment's middle star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on renwu, the moon stood nine cun from Eastern Establishment's middle star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬子，月在哭星南五寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renzi—the moon stood five cun south of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renzi, the moon stood five cun south of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，月行在東井鉞星南八寸，又在東井南轅西頭第一星南五寸，竝爲犯。

translations.literal: On xinyou—the moon traveled eight cun south of the Eastern Well halberd star, and also five cun south of the first star at the western end of the Eastern Well's southern crossbar—both encroachments.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the moon stood eight cun south of the Eastern Well halberd star and five cun south of the first star at the western end of the Eastern Well's southern crossbar—both encroachments.

sentences.zh: 進入井中。

translations.literal: It advanced into the Well.
translations.idiomatic: It advanced into the Well.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，月入太微。

translations.literal: On dingmao—the moon entered Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the moon entered Taiwei.

sentences.zh: 壬申，月行入氐，無所犯。

translations.literal: On renshen—the moon traveled into Root without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the moon entered Root without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛巳，月入羽林，又入東井曠中，又入東井北轅西頭第二星南六寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on xinsi—the moon entered the Feathered Forest, also entered the Eastern Well open center, and also entered six cun south of the second star at the western end of the Eastern Well's northern crossbar, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinsi, the moon entered the Feathered Forest and the Eastern Well open center, and advanced to six cun south of the second star at the western end of the Eastern Well's northern crossbar, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 乙未，月入太微，在右執法星東北二尺，無所犯。

translations.literal: On yiwei—the moon entered Taiwei, two chi northeast of the Right Law Administrator star, without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the moon entered Taiwei two chi northeast of the Right Law Administrator star without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，月入氐，無所犯。

translations.literal: On yihai—the moon entered Root without encroaching.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the moon entered Root without encroaching.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年正月辛亥，月入畢，在左股第一星東南一尺，爲犯。

translations.literal: Longchang year 1, first month, on xinhai—the moon entered Net, one chi southeast of the first star of the left thigh, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Longchang 1, on xinhai, the moon entered Net one chi southeast of the first star of the left thigh, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，月在東井北轅西頭第二星東七寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Third month, on xinhai—the moon stood seven cun east of the second star at the western end of the Eastern Well's northern crossbar, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinhai, the moon stood seven cun east of the second star at the western end of the Eastern Well's northern crossbar, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 甲申，月入太微，在屏星南九寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On jiashen—the moon entered Taiwei, nine cun south of the Screen Star, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the moon entered Taiwei nine cun south of the Screen Star, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，月入畢，在右股第一星東北五寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on yichou—the moon entered Net, five cun northeast of the first star of the right thigh, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yichou, the moon entered Net five cun northeast of the first star of the right thigh, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 又在歲星東南一尺，爲犯。

translations.literal: It also stood one chi southeast of Jupiter, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: It also stood one chi southeast of Jupiter, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，月入東井南轅西頭第一星東北七寸，爲犯。

translations.literal: On dingmao—the moon entered the Eastern Well, seven cun northeast of the first star at the western end of the Eastern Well's southern crossbar, an encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the moon entered the Eastern Well seven cun northeast of the first star at the western end of the Eastern Well's southern crossbar, an encroachment.

sentences.zh: 泰元元年七月，月掩心中星。

translations.literal: Taoyuan year 1, seventh month—the moon occulted the middle star of Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Taoyuan 1, seventh month: the moon occulted Heart's middle star.
